title: Why 14 is one ten and four ones
examples: Why is 14 written with a 1 and a 4?

explain.say: Have you ever wondered why fourteen is written as a 1 and a 4? Look at the board: one long rod and 4 small cubes. Together they make 14. The rod is a ten, and the cubes are ones.

draw.text: Why 14 is one ten and four ones

explain.say: Now look! Here it is in 3D: base-ten blocks. Can you see the thousand and the hundreds? Tap any part, and I will tell you about it.

draw.text: Why 14 is one ten and four ones

explain.say: This long rod is 10 little cubes stuck together in a line. We call it a ten. Instead of counting ten cubes every time, you just see one rod. How many cubes are hiding in one rod?
Now add 4 single cubes, called ones. One ten and 4 ones make 14. The 1 in 14 means one ten, and the 4 means 4 ones. Can you see why the 1 comes first?
Let us try 17. See the rod again, and now 7 cubes? One ten and 7 ones. Every number from 11 to 19 has exactly one ten. How many ones would 19 have?

You have got it! When the ones reach 10, they join into a new rod, and now there are 2 tens: 20. In Chinese, 14 is said shi si, which means ten four, so the ten is right in the name! Can you build 16?

faq.a: Teen numbers are 13 to 19, whose English names end in teen. Like 11 and 12, each one is one ten and some ones.
17 has 1 ten and 7 ones. The 1 tells you the tens, and the 7 tells you the ones.

faq.q: Why is 14 written with a 1 and a 4?
faq.a: Because the left digit counts tens and the right digit counts ones. 14 is 1 ten and 4 ones, so we write 1 then 4.

faq.q: Why do we say fourteen with the four first?
faq.a: English says the ones part first in teen names, which can be confusing. Chinese, Japanese and Korean say ten four, which matches how it is written.

faq.q: What is a base ten rod?
faq.a: It is a block made of 10 small cubes joined in a line. It shows one ten, so you can see numbers without counting every cube.
